# docs/memory/platform/

<!-- Generated by php tools/memory_index.php, except the key rules between the two marker lines, which are written by hand. -->

Server config, router, redirects, updates and TLS, system status, images and uploads, setup templates.

## Key rules

<!-- key-rules:start -->
- Pass every user-sourced value placed after `HOSTNAME` (Location, `go()`, href, `window.location`) through `pg_safe_redirect_path()`; never write your own check (`redirect-after-hostname.md`).
- Give every new outgoing cURL call `pg_curl_tls()` and `pinegrap_user_agent()` (`pg_curl_run()` does both for a fixed host); never retry without verification (`update-tls-verification.md`).
- Call `pg_post_body_discarded()` right after `init.php` in every new form-POST script, never in a JSON endpoint; compare sizes with `pg_ini_bytes()` (`upload-limits-and-empty-post.md`).
- Never call `lang()` or other `functions.php` code in `router.php`, the firewall's router phase or `get_file.php`; use `waf_text()` / `get_file_text()` (`router-no-functions-php.md`).
- Guard every function a host may disable with `function_exists()` and treat its answer as optional, above all on the install and upgrade path (`disable-functions-rule.md`).
- Touch pixels only through `pg_process_image_file()` in `includes/image_engine.php`; never open a second compression path (`image-processing-engine.md`).
- Read a picture that may be WebP with `pg_image_from_string()` or `pg_image_gd_read()`, or ask `pg_image_webp_gd_readable()` first below PHP 8.2: GD's fatal error on an animated or cut-short WebP ends the request there (`gd-webp-read.md`).
- Add a web-root server rule only to `pg_server_config_blocks()` and the default skeleton; the default must pass its own detect, and repair only adds (`server-config-web-root-rules.md`).
- Before a new door gives, zips, copies or renames a file, ask `pg_file_withheld()`; a stored name built outside `prepare_file_name()` asks `pg_file_name_reserved()` (`dkim-key-in-file-manager.md`).
- Set an optional cookie with `pg_consent_setcookie()` (keep a session copy), list it in `pg_consent_catalogue()`, hold third-party tags with `pg_consent_hold_scripts()` (`cookie-consent-new-cookies.md`).
- Use `HOSTNAME` only for answers back to the visitor; links that leave the request (mails, documents, feeds) use `HOSTNAME_SETTING` (`hostname-in-mail-links.md`).
- Make a front-end renderer whose output depends on the visitor call `pg_page_cache_personal('<why>')`, and register a header callback only through `pg_header_callback_add()` (`page-cache-gate.md`).
- Make a change to what pages show that is not a signed-in POST, a content `api.php` row, an MCP write or a `pg_announce()` call `pg_page_cache_mark_dirty()`, and sort a new designer, shared component or explorer sub-action into `pg_page_cache_panel_sub_actions()`, or the file cache serves the old page for the TTL (`page-cache-invalidation.md`).
- Cut a name a person gave (upload, archive entry, link) with `pg_basename()` and take its stem with `pg_file_name_stem()`, never `basename()` or `pathinfo()`: before PHP 8.0 they drop the non-ASCII letters the name starts with (`file-name-last-segment.md`).
- Ask `pg_dir_writable()` whether a folder takes a file, never `is_writable()`: PHP on Windows reads the folder's read-only attribute, which OneDrive and Explorer set and which stops no write (`windows-folder-is-writable.md`).
- Make a key with `pg_openssl_key_new()` and export it with the arguments it returns, never `openssl_pkey_new()` directly: without an OpenSSL config file (Windows PHP) both fail (`openssl-key-generation.md`).
- Keep a file's bytes matching its name's extension: a format change is a new file or a derivative, never a rename or rewrite in place, and the upload stays the master (`image-same-address-why.md`).
<!-- key-rules:end -->

## Files

- `INDEX.md` lists the files of this folder, one line each: search it rather than read it whole, then open only the files that match.
- `grep -i 'word' docs/memory/platform/INDEX.md`; across every folder: `grep -i 'word' docs/memory/*/INDEX.md`.
